info.title: AusAware API
info.description:
Live and recent public-safety data for Australia — fire and emergency incidents, warnings and hazards — as AusAware relays it from the agencies' own public feeds.

**Keys.** Every feed needs an API key (the reference and service endpoints are public), sent as `X-API-Key: <key>` or `Authorization: Bearer <key>`. Request one from your profile at nswpsn.forcequit.xyz (API keys); staff choose what it may read. Keys are for scripts and servers — a request carrying a browser `Origin` header is refused.

**Scopes.** A key reads an endpoint when its scopes cover the endpoint's source, type and window — listed on each operation as `x-scopes`. This document shows the public endpoints and the ones your key's scopes reach.

**Responses.** GeoJSON endpoints answer with a bare FeatureCollection. Everything else answers `{ "data": … }`. Errors are `{ "error": { "code", "message" } }` with a stable `code`.

AusAware is an independent project. It is not affiliated with, endorsed by or acting for any agency whose data it carries; the data is theirs, as published.

get.description: The latest image from a Central Watch camera — the image itself, not JSON. Images are fetched from Central Watch for every camera about every 30 seconds (less often while it is refusing) and dropped once they are about five minutes old; this answers from what has been fetched and never reads Central Watch itself. A camera with no image to hand (an unknown id, a camera offline, or one not fetched yet) answers a 640×480 SVG placeholder, also with status 200; X-Cache says which you got. Sent with headers that tell browsers not to reuse it without asking again. No key is needed.

X-Cache-Age.description: How old the image is, whole seconds. Not sent with the placeholder

get.description: Live positions of trains, metro, light rail, trams, buses and ferries inside an area, for one region, from AnyTrip. The area is clamped to the region's coverage and widened outward to a 0.01° grid; after clamping it may span at most 2.5° each way, and an area outside the region is refused. Vehicles whose last report is more than ten minutes old are left out, and at most 1,500 are returned. Each area's answer is cached for 5 seconds and can be up to 30 seconds old.
